items.title: 'Best Targets Tonight' ranks purely by transit altitude, so it recommends obscure galaxies that transit in daylight and pass through the zenith
items.summary: Confirmed at packages/skotiq_planetarium/lib/src/providers/planetarium_providers/mosaic_targets.dart:184-203 (pre-fix): calculateObjectVisibility per DSO, keep transitAltitude > 30, sort descending on transitAltitude, take 20. Nothing in that key knows where the sun is, and transit altitude is maximised at declination == latitude, so the list was permanently the same band of near-zenith objects and four of five could culminate in daylight on a panel printing sunset/sunrise six rows above. Replaced the key with a new pure module, packages/skotiq_planetarium/lib/src/planning/tonight_ranking.dart: derive tonight's darkness window from the site's own twilight (astronomical night, degrading one band at a time to nautical/civil/sun-down, null under a midnight sun), drop anything with zero usable time above 30 deg inside that window, and rank the rest with the app's OWN night scorer (TargetScoringService.scoreTargetForNight over [darkStart, darkEnd] with minAltitude 30) so the panel can no longer call a target 'best' on a key the planner and the native scheduler disagree with. No new weighting was invented: altitude, moon separation, transit timing, usable hours and airmass are the five axes already shipped and already parity-pinned against Rust. The card now headlines the hours the target is usable in darkness and the moment it peaks INSIDE that window, replacing the shared transit altitude and the daylight transit time; the section carries the subtitle 'Usable hours above 30 deg in darkness, and when each peaks' and the tooltip states the real rule. Twilight and the moon are computed inside the isolate from site+night-date, so the provider still does not depend on any per-minute provider. Measured cost on 12k DSOs: 5707 ms before, 6405 ms after (+12%), same isolate.
items.test: packages/skotiq_planetarium/test/planning/tonight_ranking_test.dart (7 cases: a zenith object culminating at 10:00 must not head the list; every ranked entry has hoursInDarkness > 0 and peaks inside the window; a never-rising object is dropped; rise/set still measured against the 30 deg floor; darknessWindowOf prefers astronomical night, degrades one band at a time, and returns null under a midnight sun) + packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/planetarium/tonight_tab_dark_hours_test.dart (the card renders '3.5h' and the in-darkness peak 10:00, and no longer renders the 15:24 transit or the 90 deg transit altitude).
items.revert_check: Replaced the body of rankTonightTargets (tonight_ranking.dart:118-208) with the pre-fix algorithm (calculateObjectVisibility, keep transitAltitude > 30, sort descending on transitAltitude, take 20). 'a target that only culminates in daylight cannot head the list' failed with Expected <1> / Actual <0>, and 'every ranked target has usable time inside the darkness window' failed on the peak-time-inside-window assertion. Restored; all 7 pass.

items.title: Search hint badge reads '⌘K' on Linux and Windows, where the shortcut is Ctrl+K
items.summary: Confirmed: hardcoded Apple Command glyph at packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/planetarium/widgets/redesign/command_bar.dart:198 and (as the escape \u2318) packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/planetarium/widgets/search_header.dart:670, on every platform, while the handler accepts Meta OR Control. Added packages/skotiq_ui/lib/src/utils/platform_shortcuts.dart with shortcutLabel(key) -> 'Ctrl+K' on Linux/Windows/Android/Fuchsia and '⌘K' on macOS/iOS, exported from the skotiq_ui barrel, and used at both sites.
items.test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/planetarium/search_shortcut_badge_platform_test.dart — pumps the real SearchHeader under debugDefaultTargetPlatformOverride for linux/windows/macOS and asserts the rendered badge, plus a pure check of the helper. (The override is cleared inside the test body; flutter_test asserts foundation debug vars are unset before tearDown runs.)
items.revert_check: Put the literal '\u2318K' back at search_header.dart:670. 'desktop Linux advertises Ctrl+K' and 'Windows advertises Ctrl+K' both failed; macOS still passed. Restored; all 4 pass.

items.title: Object search has no exact-designation path: typing a catalogue number returns 175 fuzzy matches
items.kind: A - objectively wrong (ranking); the fuzzy-tail cap left alone as taste
items.summary: Root cause found in the data, not just the ranking: OpenNGC's Identifiers column is loaded wholesale into DeepSkyObject.catalogIds (packages/skotiq_planetarium/lib/src/catalogs/catalog.dart:198-208), and those cross-identifiers are zero-padded — NGC7107 carries 'PGC 067209', NGC7112 'PGC 067208', IC5118 'PGC 067202', IC728 'UGC 06720'. _scoreMatch scored a typed '6720' as a plain SUBSTRING match against all of them, so every one tied with NGC6720 itself at score 2 and the ONLY thing that put M57 first was the brightness tie-break — i.e. the right answer was luck, and a fainter true match would lose. Added designation-aware ranking in packages/skotiq_planetarium/lib/src/providers/planetarium_providers/object_search.dart: _splitDesignation parses 'prefix + number' (ignoring zero padding and spacing, and refusing composite survey ids like '2MASX J...' or 'ESO 287-052'), and an exact designation match scores -1, above every _scoreMatch band. A PREFIXED query pins the catalogue ('UGC 6720' answers IC728, not NGC6720); a BARE number is honoured only for M/NGC/IC, deliberately narrow so '6720' cannot promote HD 6720 — that would have replaced one wrong first result with another. This also fixes Enter/fly-to (resolveBest returns results.first).
items.test: packages/skotiq_planetarium/test/search_designation_ranking_test.dart — 5 cases with a deliberately BRIGHTER UGC/PGC decoy so the brightness tie-break cannot be what wins: bare '6720' resolves NGC6720; Enter/fly-to resolves it; a bright HD6720 star is not promoted by a bare number; prefixed queries pin the catalogue (UGC/PGC/HD/NGC); zero padding and spacing are irrelevant.
items.revert_check: Set _exactDesignationScore from -1 to 2 (the substring band). 3 of 5 cases failed — '6720' resolved to the brighter HD6720 instead of NGC6720. Restored; all 5 pass, and the pre-existing test/search_resolver_test.dart (9 cases) still passes.
items.not_done: The finding also asked to cap the fuzzy tail and stop counting it in the headline count. The remaining 169 hits are genuine substring matches on HIP/HD ids, they now rank below the exact match, and the omnibox already sections results by object class. Where to cut a legitimate-but-noisy tail is a product call, so it was left alone rather than guessed at.

items.title: The one layer that makes imaging-scale fields usable - DSS survey imagery - is off by default and buried in a panel
items.summary: The finding is factually right — at a 2 deg field the bundled HYG catalog draws roughly 3 stars per square degree and the chart is effectively empty for framing, and the DSS layer that fixes it is three clicks deep. But the current default is a DELIBERATE, documented decision, not an oversight: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/planetarium/widgets/redesign/layers_panel.dart:55-59 states 'Needs the internet, hence off by default and labelled with the zoom it engages at, so an offline user is not left wondering why a switch they flipped did nothing.' Flipping it changes what the app does on first launch — a Pi at a dark site on a phone hotspot would start fetching survey tiles the moment the operator zooms in, with no consent. That is a decision about what the product is, so it is reported, not taken.
items.options: (a) Default the layer ON (it already self-limits to FOV < 8 deg) and keep a 'uses network' note: matches NINA's framing assistant and Telescopius, and the planetarium is instantly usable for framing — but the app makes network requests nobody asked for, which costs data on a tethered field rig and fails silently offline. (b) Leave it OFF but offer it once, in place, the first time the user zooms past the catalog's depth ('This field is beyond the bundled catalog — load DSS imagery?'), remembering the answer: no silent network, and the layer becomes discoverable at exactly the moment it matters — but it is one more prompt, and a user who dismisses it is back where they started. (c) Leave as-is and only improve the label.
items.recommendation: (b). It closes the real defect — discoverability at framing scale — without overriding the owner's stated offline-first reasoning, and it puts the offer at the only moment the operator can judge it: when the chart in front of them has run out of stars.

items.title: Region detail opens on a viewport-filling empty preview with no empty state; everything informative is below the fold
items.summary: Confirmed at packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/your_sky/region_detail_screen.dart:219-231 (pre-fix): a free AspectRatio(3/2) hero, so on a 1600x900 window it rendered ~1030px tall — taller than the viewport — with a bare grey Container and one icon when there are no folds. Everything that says anything sat below the fold, and the ListView did not even build it. Two cause fixes: the preview is now sized by a LayoutBuilder to min(width * 2/3, 320) so the card's own coordinate line and the sections under it stay on a standard desktop window (BoxFit.cover crops rather than distorts, and on a phone the cap never binds), and the empty state is now words inside the preview ('Nothing imaged here yet' + 'Point a session at this patch of sky and its frames fold in here.'), matching how the parent Your Sky screen handles the same state. Fixing the height exposed a pre-existing RenderFlex overflow in the growth card's empty placeholder — AdaptiveChartContainer.fixed(height: 170) clipped an EmptyState.compact that needs more once narrowed to its 360px column (it would already stripe on a phone today) — so that box became a minHeight floor instead of a fixed height.
items.test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/your_sky/region_detail_empty_state_test.dart — pumps RegionDetailScreen at 1600x900 with an empty region and asserts both empty-state sentences render, the coordinate line sits above y=430, and 'Contributing frames' is built and above y=900. Also gates the overflow: the test fails on any thrown FlutterError.
items.revert_check: Restored the AspectRatio(3/2) + bare-icon preview. The test failed immediately — 'Found 0 widgets with text "Nothing imaged here yet"'. Before the growth-card fix the same test failed on 'A RenderFlex overflowed by 38 pixels' from the placeholder. Restored; the whole your_sky suite (35 cases) passes.

collateral: TargetCard's display slots were renamed from altitude/transit to metric/caption (packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/planetarium/widgets/sidebar_shared_widgets.dart) because the catalog tab already passed 'mag' through the 'transit' slot; the trailing column is now bounded to 96px with single-line ellipsis, which closes a real narrow-sidebar overflow the wider caption exposed at 300px.
pre_existing_failures: packages/skotiq_planetarium/test/benchmark/golden_compare_test.dart fails on Linux (00-wide-start maxDelta=218 changed=4.43%, limit 0.20%). Sky-renderer goldens are Windows-captured and sky_renderer.dart was already modified in the working tree before this task; nothing in this change touches the render path.
